channel.title: JDU
channel.description: Thoughts on software, systems, architecture, and experiences.

item.title: What I Want to Build
item.description: A moral dilemma about relying on LLMs to build the humanitarian and knowledge-management tools I actually want to build, versus the cost to my own integrity and understanding.

item.title: Part 5: Bringing It to People
item.description: Part 5 of the UDA series — on the tools being built to operationalize the system and bring it to the people who use it.

item.title: UDA Addendum: Frequently Asked Questions
item.description: A collection of frequently asked questions about the UDA series.

item.title: UDA Addendum: Giving Thanks
item.description: A closing note to the UDA series, acknowledging the engineers, researchers, and decades of published work on ontologies, knowledge graphs, and semantic data platforms it stands on — plus a reading list for anyone who wants to go deeper.

item.title: Part 6: The Organisation as a Graph
item.description: On what happens once concepts, relationships, and mappings become operational — the organisation turns into something you can navigate directly, through time as well as structure, instead of something you reverse-engineer from tables.

item.title: Part 3: Once Meaning Exists
item.description: On what becomes derivable once an organisation's meaning is described well enough — generated GraphQL and REST APIs, warehouse tables, query engines, and an integration spine that doesn't care which system sits behind it.

item.title: Part 3: When Meaning Becomes Operational
item.description: Part 3 of the UDA series — on why an ontology only earns its keep once software depends on it, and how mappings, projections, lineage, and governance all fall out of meaning instead of storage.

item.title: Part 2: Building a Language for the Organisation
item.description: Part 2 of the UDA series — on describing an organisation with nouns before tables, and why concepts, attributes, and relationships exist before any database does.

item.title: Part 1: Data Isn't Reality
item.description: Part 1 of a series on data, ontologies, and data architecture — on why data isn't reality but a representation of it, and why a recorded value only becomes data once it claims to describe something in the real world.

item.title: Evolving
item.description: On why architecture in organisations that constantly reinvent themselves should be judged by how little effort it takes to become something new — and how adaptive architecture, Praxeme, and sustainment thinking get you there.

item.title: Build the Line
item.description: Reflections on wildfire crews and what they reveal about quality, teamwork, and how things actually get done when systems are imperfect and people are tired.

item.title: Important Update: Strategic Modernisation of Data Services
item.description: An announcement on the phased retirement of the data lake, warehouses, and ingestion pipelines in favour of a more intentional, catalogue-based operating model.

item.title: Pens & Paper
item.description: A meditation on the pleasures and frustrations of finding the right pen and paper combination, and why it matters.

item.title: Slipbox: Version 1.0
item.description: An exploration of note-taking systems, why digital apps fall short, and the journey to building a physical slipbox.

item.title: Frozen Insight in a Moving World
item.description: An exploration of the divide between AI optimists and sceptics, and why our beliefs about AI adoption are misaligned with how society actually absorbs new technologies.

item.title: Idioms
item.description: An evolving collection of engineering idioms, principles, and laws to keep in mind when designing and building software systems.

item.title: Ice
item.description: A personal recounting of falling through the ice at age 15 in Northern Ontario, and lessons about respecting the environment you live in.

item.title: git Worktrees
item.description: An introduction to git worktrees — an underused feature that makes context switching between branches faster and less painful.

item.title: Working From Home
item.description: Practical tips, tricks, and motivation for working from home, drawn from 10+ years of remote work experience across multiple countries.

item.title: Method Madness
item.description: A primer on basic programming concepts, exploring how to write cleaner, more readable, and more intentional code.
